blocks.text: ComposerView captures text and owns transient composition events. DraftStore persists account- and conversation-scoped unsent input without control-local IME state. AttachmentCoordinator exposes finalized asset IDs. TurnCoordinator snapshots one send command and reduces echoed message plus stream events. MessageList consumes current-turn selectors and an abstract paged history source.

Boundary checks:
- Draft state never masquerades as a sent message.
- One command correlates optimistic user row and assistant stream.
- Attachment readiness is explicit.
- AbortSignal stops local transport work; terminal truth still reconciles.
- History remains a UI-facing paged contract.

blocks.title: Core building blocks
rows: ComposerView
Text, IME events, shortcuts, autosize, and focus
Keeps native input semantics at the interaction boundary.
DraftStore
Scopes and persists unsent text, excluding transient IME state
Allows navigation recovery without serializing mounted-control state or writing conversation history.
TurnCoordinator
Owns send command, optimistic row, stream sequence, and terminal reconciliation
Prevents late data from crossing turns.
AttachmentCoordinator
Tracks local, uploading, ready, and failed attachments
Send includes only finalized asset IDs.
StreamAdapter
Parses lowercase SSE fields and exposes typed sequenced events
Transport parsing stays outside components.

blocks.code:
ComposerView (transient IME interaction)
  -> DraftStore (account + conversation + text revision)
  -> AttachmentCoordinator (local file -> finalized asset ID)
  -> TurnCoordinator (command ID + client message ID)
  -> ChatTurnClient (send + resume + stable Stop + snapshot)
  -> StreamAdapter (stream ID + message ID + sequence)
  -> Current-turn reducer
  -> MessageList and restrained status announcements

blocks.title: Composer and stream decisions
items: DraftStore owns recoverable unsent text; ComposerView owns transient composition state.
TurnCoordinator owns one command and assistant placeholder.
Streaming deltas append only when stream identity and sequence match.
Stop reuses one stable command identity, preserves partial text, and reconciles the authoritative terminal phase.

blocks.title: Composer and current-turn failure patterns
items: Multiple components mutating message state independently.
Streaming chunks appended to a new message each time.
No cancel path for long responses.
Loading the full history every time without pagination.

steps.title: 1. Restore
steps.text: Render recent messages and restore the scoped draft independently.

steps.title: 2. Send
steps.text: Snapshot a composition-complete draft, finalized attachment IDs, command ID, and client message ID.

steps.title: 3. Stream
steps.text: Open the stream, append chunks to the assistant message, and update status.

steps.title: 4. Reconcile
steps.text: Merge echoed message identity and terminal stream state through the current-turn reducer.

steps.title: 5. Resume
steps.text: On reload or reconnect, resume events after the last accepted sequence; if the cursor cannot continue, fetch an authoritative turn snapshot and reconcile it by conversation, command, message, and stream identity.

items.label: State ownership
items.helperText: Unsent intent and sent turn have different owners.

items.label: Persistence
items.helperText: History implementation stays outside the frontend design.

blocks.title: Composer and stream ownership
blocks.text: Keep native, transient composition behavior in the view, account-scoped local intent in DraftStore, asynchronous turn identity in TurnCoordinator, and raw protocol parsing in StreamAdapter.
Worked example: Enter during IME composition followed by cancel

A Japanese input method is composing text when Enter is pressed, then the user submits the completed prompt with an attachment and cancels the streaming response. Keyboard shortcuts must respect composition and cancellation must not erase the sent turn.

blocks.title: Scenario walkthrough
rows: Enter during composition
Observe composition state and do not submit.
The IME commits or selects text normally.
Shortcut does not corrupt input.
Composition ends
Update the draft and validated attachment references.
Autosize follows measured content within bounds.
Draft is one coherent value.
User sends
Create a client message ID and pending send command, then clear only after local snapshot.
Message appears pending and composer resets safely.
Sent content remains recoverable.
User stops stream
Create one stable Stop command, abort local reading, and retain received text as partial while authoritative status reconciles.
Stop becomes Retry or Continue by product policy.
Local cancellation is not proof of server cancellation or message deletion.
